A small republic in Central Europe. Electricity is scarce, the Halvek border is watched. The Ministry of National Security keeps a file on every citizen, and in the streets the Militia arrests whoever it is pointed at.
Inspecteur de 3e classe, premier jour à: Inspector, 3rd class, first day at Section 4. Your father was a licensed clockmaker: he set the clocks of the railway station and the ministries. In 1971 his licence was withdrawn, and then he disappeared without explanation. As a rule, the Ministry does not hire the son of a man who fell from favour. It took you. Nobody has told you why.
Chaque jour, des dossiers de citoyens si: Every day, files on citizens who have been reported. Read the documents, note what matters, and look for two items that do not say the same thing: that is a contradiction.
Une journée de service dure huit heures,: A working day lasts eight hours, from 08h00 to 16h00. Reading a document, noting it, comparing two items: that is free. But interrogating, searching a home, requesting an archive or consulting your superior costs hours. You can pull up to two hours of overtime — at the cost of your evening. You cannot do everything on every file: choosing where to dig is already a decision. When your day is over, click END OF SHIFT, at the bottom right of the screen.
Vous signez ensuite une conclusion. Derr: You then sign a conclusion. Behind every file there is someone: an archive will show you their fate — transferred, released, deported — and sometimes a line from their family. Choosing well means weighing the evidence AND what it costs a human being. The VERITAS system will advise you. It is not always right.
